research_question: How should RSI design a deterministic, revision-aware structural codegraph and safely federate it with episodic knowledge?

findings.summary: D5 is an unsliced benchmark-gated codegraph idea that this design must refine.
The May 11 project-scoped memory plan is implemented history, not active planning.
Workflow DAGs, episodic memory, and structural code truth require separate models and lifecycles.
Effective sandbox or worktree identity determines the source structure visible to a session.
Deterministic tree-sitter extraction is valuable, but RSI needs exact spans and versioned rules.
Dictionary and JSON graph storage weakens typing, parallel-edge preservation, and multi-evidence fidelity.
Structural facts need explicit provenance, numeric confidence, producer identity, and source evidence.
Changed and deleted file contributions require transactional replacement and stale-edge elimination.
Every graph query requires uniform count, depth, time, memory, and token budgets.
Deterministic document markers belong in structure while LLM rationale belongs in evidence-labelled federation.
Node summaries are derived model output requiring provenance and invalidation, not structural truth.
A dense native inspector has MVP value; broad visualization and export should follow demand.
Work-memory overlays must remain separate from structure and become governed federation links.
Multi-repository graphs require namespaced identity, authorized scope, and explicit cross-repository evidence.
Later upstream fixes reinforce identity, staleness, ambiguity, direction, and scope as invariants.
Per-workspace SQLite structure plus durable main-database links best balances churn, recovery, and knowledge durability.
Tree-sitter plus Cargo metadata is the lowest-risk Rust, Cargo, and Markdown MVP base.
rust-analyzer and SCIP should be optional measured precision augmentations, not MVP coupling.
Bounded SQL plus bounded in-memory snapshots is the appropriate traversal split.
Community detection should be a later derived benchmark rather than an MVP dependency.
Dreamer source_ids must remain observation lineage; cross-domain relationships need a separate ledger.
Native tool registries already demonstrate server-bound project and caller authorization.
Dormant FileIndex and RetrievalBackend concepts provide an integration seam without model collapse.
Codegraph retrieval should be on demand rather than unconditionally injected into session context.
Daemon indexing requires bounded queues, debounce, cancellation, backpressure, reconciliation, and health.
Existing dense navigator and inspector overlays provide an appropriate native TUI grammar.
Before-and-after benchmarks and evidence-correct golden questions must gate expansion beyond dogfood.

open_questions.summary: Should initial indexing be explicit opt-in or automatic only for the RSI dogfood repository?
What clean and dirty snapshot retention limits should apply per worktree?
May a future slice add the durable federation ledger to main rsi.db?
Should the first implementation slice include TUI inspection or daemon and native tools only?
